clue.text: Most unusual storing data setting for Amazon, say

indicators.note: something storing goods holds them inside it, so one word is kept within the other

blocks.note: rarest means most unusual
info is short for information, i.e. data

explanation.surface: Something about an exotic data centre being set up for the online retailer Amazon.
explanation.walkthrough: Amazon looks like the online company storing data, but it is the South American river; 'say' flags it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazon river runs through the vast tropical jungle of South America, which is its setting.

clue.text: Called and spoke

blocks.note: first meaning: telephoned
second meaning: a crossbar or ... of a ladder, chair or wheel

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoke' reads as the past of speak, matching 'Called'; it is the noun for a bar or step.
explanation.definitionFit: Past participle of ring, meaning phoned; and a noun for a ladder's step, which a spoke also is.

clue.text: Maybe burgle independent theatre, committing offence

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for independent
NT is the National Theatre in London
something rude gives offence

explanation.surface: A burglar breaks into an independent theatre and commits a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Burglary is one example of trespassing on property, so 'maybe' marks burgle as one instance of the verb.

clue.text: Instead of proposed refund it swapped bad apples

indicators.note: letters that are swapped around end up in a new order

blocks.note: 'for' can mean in place of
to bid is to propose an offer; bid is also its past tense
these eight letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A shopper refuses a refund and swaps the rotten apples instead.
explanation.walkthrough: The apple Eve took in Eden is the original example: bad in the sense of prohibited, not rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the apple of Eden that God banned, extended to any illicit temptation.

clue.text: Promise not to be unfaithful again?

definitions.text: Promise not to be unfaithful again?

blocks.clueFragment: Promise not to be unfaithful again?
blocks.note: surface reading: someone caught cheating swears never to stray a second time

blocks.clueFragment: Promise not to be unfaithful again?
blocks.note: setter's reading: make the marriage vow of fidelity for a second time, at a new wedding

explanation.walkthrough: 'Again' seems to attach to being unfaithful; it really attaches to the promise, i.e. a second wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedding vows include a pledge of fidelity, so taking them a second time is wedding anew.

clue.text: Spades also remove the stones from play area

blocks.note: S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades
and means also
to pit fruit is to take out its stones

explanation.surface: Gardeners use spades to clear stones from a children's play area.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's playground often has a box of sand to dig in, a recreational enclosure for toddlers.

clue.text: Ball beats me!

blocks.note: first meaning: a kick or throw of the ball to a teammate
second meaning: what a quiz contestant says when stumped

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation suggests someone bested at a ball game; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a ball sent to a teammate is a pass; and 'I pass' is what you say when you cannot answer.

clue.text: Mother in AA not losing love for the hard stuff

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it
losing something means it drops out, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: taken as written; opened to hold the next piece
a dam is an animal's mother
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A mother in Alcoholics Anonymous still craving spirits, 'the hard stuff'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The hard stuff' means strong liquor in the surface, but the answer is the legendary hardest substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant is the name for a mythical substance of unbreakable hardness, often equated with diamond.

clue.text: Son has one meal after another, then seconds, showing determination

indicators.note: one thing after another comes second, so the piece before this word is placed later

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
another meal: tea, the evening meal in much of Britain
to dine is to have a meal
S is the abbreviation for second, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A greedy son eats meal after meal and goes back for seconds, determined to clear the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has one meal after another' places the verb meaning eat after a second meal; 'seconds' are not second helpings but two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadiness here is firmness of purpose, a resolve that does not waver.

clue.text: Cyclops a touch poorly beginning to suspect bug

indicators.note: poorly means unwell or done badly, so the letters are put out of order
the beginning of a word is its first letter alone

blocks.note: these thirteen letters go into the mix
the first letter of suspect

explanation.surface: The one-eyed giant feels a bit unwell and suspects he has caught a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: A bug is everyday slang for an infection or the germ causing it; this genus of bacteria is a common one.

clue.text: Clear screen

blocks.note: first meaning: earn as profit after deductions
second meaning: a mesh used as a barrier or sieve

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like a computer command; each word is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear a sum is to make it as profit after costs; and a mesh curtain or barrier is a kind of screen.

clue.text: Object's engineers battle time and cost

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
Mons, in Belgium, was a First World War battle
T is the abbreviation for time
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: A list of an object's engineering, battle, time and cost, like a military budget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' reads as a noun with the 's; it is the verb meaning to protest.
explanation.definitionFit: To remonstrate is to protest forcefully, the verb sense of object.

clue.text: Bandage major laceration on Tuesday

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another sits after it, so the earlier words are placed second

blocks.note: TU is a short form for Tuesday
a big rip is a major tear

explanation.surface: Someone got a big cut on Tuesday and needs it dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: Tubigrip is a British brand of elasticated tubular bandage; in an across clue 'on' puts the tear after the day.
explanation.definitionFit: The brand name is a stretchy tube of fabric used as a support dressing for sprains.

clue.text: Penny slept with tartan blanket

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for a penny
slang: laid means had sex with

explanation.surface: Penny went to bed under a tartan blanket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a woman's name but gives a coin abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaid is a long checked woollen cloth worn over the shoulder in Highland dress, or a rug of it.

clue.text: Pro bottles shot in deep trap

indicators.note: something shot is wrecked, so these letters are out of their original order

blocks.note: these ten letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: A professional golfer flubs a shot into a deep bunker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pro bottles' looks like the pro losing nerve, and 'shot' a stroke; both are mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: This basket-like cage is lowered to the seabed to catch crustaceans, a trap set in the deep.

clue.text: Work always covering term time for school inspectors?

indicators.note: something covering another wraps round it, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: OP is short for opus, a work
ay is an old or poetic word for ever
a term can be an end or limit

explanation.surface: A busy period of work, inspectors always present during school term.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'school inspectors' are not Ofsted officials but parents and children looking round; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A school's day for visitors lets prospective families look round, so they become informal inspectors.

clue.text: Stretch things as far as possible, tailor's suggestion?

definitions.text: Stretch things as far as possible

blocks.clueFragment: Stretch things as far as possible
blocks.note: first meaning: British idiom for testing how much one can get away with
second meaning: what a tailor says when offering a garment for a fitting

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stretch' suggests fabric, linking to the tailor; the first meaning is a British idiom for being cheeky or chancing it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means push one's luck, and literally invites a customer to put on clothing to check its fit.

clue.text: Navy uniform in stock provides chest brace

indicators.note: being in something means placed inside it

blocks.note: RN is the Royal Navy
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet
a stock is a stem or trunk, as in a plant's main stalk

explanation.surface: The navy keeps uniforms in stock, including a brace for the chest.
explanation.definitionFit: The breastbone is the flat bone at the front of the ribcage that holds the ribs together, a brace for the chest.

clue.text: Dishes from Lent essentially ashes?

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only its central letters are kept

blocks.note: the two middle letters of Lent
ash is a tree, so ashes are an example of trees; the question mark flags this

explanation.surface: Meals during Lent are basically ashes, as on Ash Wednesday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ashes' points to Ash Wednesday, which begins Lent, but it means the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrees are courses served at a meal, either a main course or a starter, so they are plates of food.

clue.text: Fellow setter out cycling shows spirit

indicators.note: cycling moves round in a loop, so the front letter goes round to the back

blocks.note: a fellow is a man
the setter refers to themself as I
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fellow crossword setter is out on a bike and in good spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the first letter of 'out' to the end gives the last three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Among Algonquian peoples this is a supernatural power or spirit pervading nature.

clue.text: Cub leader has grease around head

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: oil is grease
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: The leader of a Cub Scout pack has greased-back hair.
explanation.walkthrough: Cub leader suggests Akela of the Cub Scouts; here the cubs are young lions, and the mother leads them.
explanation.definitionFit: A female lion raises and guides her young, the cubs of a pride.

clue.text: Burning carbon slowing down in novel analysis

blocks.note: lit means set alight
C is the chemical symbol for carbon
rit. is ritardando, the musical direction to slow down

explanation.surface: Burning carbon slowing in a new kind of chemical analysis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new; here it is a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is informal shorthand for literary criticism, the study of fiction such as a novel.

clue.text: Illustration needs a little help, Max Ernst reflected

indicators.note: only a little of the phrase is used, a run of letters lying within it
a reflection shows things mirror-wise, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling these words

explanation.surface: The surrealist painter Max Ernst needs a little help with an illustration.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance that shows what is meant serves to illustrate it, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Tenants denied outside access

indicators.note: being denied the outside means losing the letters at both ends

blocks.note: renters are people who pay to occupy a property

explanation.surface: Tenants are refused access from outside the building.
explanation.definitionFit: To access a place is to go into it, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Speculative citizen swaps an ace for nothing

indicators.note: to swap one thing for another is to exchange it, replacing a letter

blocks.note: a national is a citizen of a country
A is the abbreviation for ace
nothing is zero, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A citizen gambling at cards trades an ace for nothing, a speculative move.
explanation.definitionFit: Something notional exists only in theory or estimate, which is to say hypothetical.

clue.text: A river that's partly blue, almost indigo

indicators.note: almost all of something means its final letter is left off

blocks.note: taken as written
the Blue Nile is one of the two main branches of this river

explanation.surface: A river with blue patches, nearly indigo in colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partly blue' seems to describe a colour; it means the river has a branch called Blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil is the West Indian indigo plant, and the dark-blue dye made from it.

clue.text: Old rich Tories drunk on power

indicators.note: drunk people stagger about, so these letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for power
these ten letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Elderly wealthy Conservatives intoxicated by their own power.
explanation.walkthrough: Tories are members of Britain's Conservative Party; 'Old' seems to describe them but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Prehistoric means from before written records, and informally means extremely ancient or outdated.

clue.text: Fix geometric ratio with any number

blocks.note: pi is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter
N stands for an unspecified number in algebra

explanation.surface: Instructions to fix a ratio in geometry using any number you like.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix something in place with a fastener is to pin it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: American drunkard turns to fighting dog

indicators.note: something that turns round faces the other way, so it is read backwards

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
a sot is a habitual drunk

explanation.surface: A drunken American takes up dogfighting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tosa is a Japanese mastiff breed bred for dog fighting, banned in Britain.

clue.text: Only a balloon, thank goodness

blocks.note: just means only
taken as written
to balloon is to swell

explanation.surface: Relief that it was only a balloon bursting, not a gunshot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balloon' looks like a noun but is the verb meaning to expand.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase expresses relief that things turned out fortunately, much like an exclamation of gratitude.
